senses.sense_definition: To adapt a wild animal or plant to live in close association with humans.

examples.text: Humans began to <w>domesticate</w> wolves thousands of years ago.
It is difficult to <w>domesticate</w> wild animals that are not used to human contact.

senses.sense_definition: To make someone or something more accustomed to a quiet, settled home life.

examples.text: He tried to <w>domesticate</w> his wild lifestyle after getting married.
They are slowly <w>domesticating</w> each other by spending quiet evenings at home.

senses.sense_definition: To adapt a text or cultural product to fit the norms and expectations of a local culture.

examples.text: The translator chose to <w>domesticate</w> the novel to make it more accessible to local readers.
Critics argued that the film was too heavily <w>domesticated</w> for the international market.

senses.sense_definition: To make a legal document valid and enforceable in a different jurisdiction.

examples.text: The lawyer had to <w>domesticate</w> the foreign court order before it could be enforced here.
You must <w>domesticate</w> the judgment in this state to collect the debt.

senses.sense_definition: An animal or plant that has been adapted to live with humans.

examples.text: The farm is home to many different <w>domesticates</w> including cows and sheep.
Researchers study the genetic history of various <w>domesticates</w> to understand human migration.
